package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

// A var declaration whose initializer spells a function value by name binds
// the same closure the short declaration binds.

func f(x int) string { return fmt.Sprint("f", x) }

type T int

func (t T) M() string   { return fmt.Sprint("M", int(t)) }
func (t *T) P() string  { return fmt.Sprint("P", int(*t)) }
func callRecover() bool { return recover() != nil }

type S struct{ *T }

type Box[T any] struct{ V T }

func (b Box[T]) Get() T { return b.V }

var (
	fn      = f
	fnTyped func(int) string = f
	lit                      = func(x int) string { return fmt.Sprint("lit", x) }
	seven   T                = 7
	bound                    = seven.M
	expr                     = T.M
	ptrExpr                  = (*T).P
	wrapper                  = S.M
	generic                  = Box[string]{V: "boxed"}.Get
)

func mustPanic(g func()) (recovered bool) {
	defer func() { recovered = recover() != nil }()
	g()
	return
}

func main() {
	var local = f
	fmt.Println(fn(1), fnTyped(2), lit(3), local(4))
	fmt.Println(bound(), expr(seven), ptrExpr(&seven), wrapper(S{&seven}), generic())
	var deferred = f
	defer func() { fmt.Println("deferred", deferred(5)) }()
	// A deferred call through a package-level function variable.
	fmt.Println(mustPanic(func() {
		var recoverer = callRecover
		defer recoverer()
		panic("x")
	}))
	// Positive control: the short-declaration form.
	short := f
	fmt.Println(short(6))
	os.Exit(3)
}
